data.narrative:
Dispatcher is a Defense & Security frontier-tech company founded by Nick Clouse and Maxwell Wang. The analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 peers: 2 publicly traded firms (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems. Stage and current valuation remain undisclosed, as does total capital raised.

The peer-median method was determined inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. Of 23 same-sector peers identified in Defense & Security, zero met simultaneous filters for identical stage, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation-tier similarity. The threshold for statistical reliability—a minimum of three datapoints—could not be satisfied within any filtered cohort. Attempting to default to all-sector medians would introduce material bias given the structural and capital intensity differences across vertical markets.

Given the methodological constraints, a reliable quantitative valuation range cannot be derived from the data supplied. Proceeding responsibly requires either: (1) expanding the comparable set to include adjacent defense subsectors with stage alignment; (2) obtaining additional financial metrics (revenue, runway, capital deployed) from existing peers to proxy stage maturity; or (3) reverting to venture-stage benchmarking frameworks outside comparable multiples. Key uncertainties center on whether Dispatcher's stage and scale align with the public-market Defense & Security peers or with earlier-stage private capital structures. Additional diligence on peer capital deployment and product maturity is warranted before triangulation.
